$comment: One brand, everywhere. The palette the web app and the public site draw with, the
palette the PDF and the workbook draw with, the wordmarks, and the handful of
sentences that name a vendor rather than state a fact.
Selected at run time by the Brand setting, so one image serves both and switching is
a restart rather than a rebuild. The same shape as brands/<id>.json in the Dynamics
365 Contact Center estimator, which is where this idea came from.
What is NOT in here: anything true regardless of the colours. Where the product runs,
whose subscription holds the database and whose account signs you in are facts about
the deployment, and a brand file that could change them would be a brand file that
could make the privacy page lie.
name: Capgemini
$rampComment: The ramp every other token is derived from. The stylesheets define this same set as
their built-in default, so a missing or failed /brand.css leaves the product looking
like this rather than looking like nothing.
The family names are roles, not hues: blue is the primary, lightblue the secondary,
turquoise the tertiary. A brand whose primary is purple still fills blue-600.
$pdfComment: The report and the workbook. Separate from the ramp because print is not screen: the
cover band and the chart series are chosen for paper and for a projector, and the
series has to stay distinguishable in greyscale.
$copyComment: The sentences that name a vendor. Everything else in the product's text is the same
whoever ships it, and lives in the localisation bundles where it belongs.

copy.preparedBy: Prepared by Capgemini. Estimates are ranges from a rule catalogue, not a quotation.
copy.coverAlt: Report cover with the Capgemini wordmark and the headline figures
